definitions: The specific time intervals or durations (e.g., daily, hourly, weekly) that a particular system, platform, or analysis tool is designed to process, display, or operate with for financial or other time-series data.
The range of discrete time units that a charting or data analysis application can effectively handle and present.
examples: The trading platform's documentation lists all supported bar periods.
Ensure your analysis uses one of the supported bar periods for accurate results.
The software update expanded the supported bar periods to include 1-minute intervals.
